claim: Umbrel's web UI is React 19 + Vite 6 + Tailwind 4 with Radix primitives and the tRPC 11 client
Umbrel's UI sends tRPC subscriptions over WebSocket always, and queries/mutations over WebSocket when a token exists, falling back to HTTP with a Bearer token
Umbrel launches an app by opening a new browser tab at the box hostname plus the app's own port (or its onion address over Tor); apps are not embedded in the dashboard
Umbrel notifications are plain strings kept in umbreld's store, scoped per account, and pushed to open UIs through an internal event bus; no phone push path exists in this module
Umbrel allows at most 3 home-screen widgets per account; app widgets are visible only to the owner and members the app is shared with
umbreld runs as a host systemd service (umbrel.service, Restart=always) ordered after docker and libvirt, outside any container runtime
Umbrel onboarding steps in the UI are: create account, storage selection (external drive, RAID), and restore from backup
Umbrel links its own iOS and Android apps from the Photos add-source dialog (phone photo backup)
Olares app windows: openMethod accepts default, iframe or window; iframe opens the app inside a desktop window, window opens a browser tab; default is iframe
Olares gives every app entrance its own subdomain under the user's Olares ID domain (e.g. vault.<user>.olares.com) and forces an Envoy sidecar onto entrance pods for authn/authz

LarePass (package @didvault/app 1.10.30) is one Vue 3 + Quasar codebase shipped as Capacitor 7 mobile apps (push-notifications, FCM, barcode scanner, BLE) and an Electron 39 desktop app with auto-update
Olares documents built-in reverse-proxy access through Cloudflare Tunnel and FRP so every app can have its own domain
Home Assistant frontend (Apache-2.0) is Lit 3 web components talking to Core over the home-assistant-js-websocket client, with a Workbox service worker
HA onboarding screens include create user, restore backup, location/core config, analytics opt-in and integrations
HA Companion apps are separate native codebases: iOS in Swift, Android in Kotlin, both Apache-2.0
HA Companion remote push uses Google Firebase Cloud Messaging; limit 500 notifications per device per day; notification contents are not encrypted on FCM

HA Local Push delivers notifications over the WebSocket API instead of APNs/FCM; on iOS only when on the internal URL with configured SSIDs; macOS keeps a connection while the app runs; Android needs a persistent notification
HA Core repairs use an issue registry with severities critical/error/warning, an is_fixable flag and a learn-more URL

Home Assistant is removing its global 'Advanced mode' profile toggle, described as one binary switch gating unrelated features; show_advanced_options is deprecated (always True) and removed in Core 2027.6; authors should group extra options in sections instead
CasaOS-UI (Apache-2.0, latest release v0.4.25 2025-09-26) is built on Vue 2.7.16 with Buefy

Homarr (homarr-labs/homarr) is Apache-2.0, release v2.12.0 (2026-11-06), built with Next.js 16 and tRPC 11, with about 50 integration modules (Home Assistant, Proxmox, TrueNAS, Unraid, Pi-hole, Jellyfin, ntfy, Gotify, Uptime Kuma and others) and a custom-widgets package
Dashboard project licences (GitHub API, 2026-11-11): Homepage GPL-3.0 (v2.7.0), Glance AGPL-3.0 (v0.8.8), Dashy MIT (4.9.0), Heimdall MIT (v2.8.4)
ntfy is dual-licensed Apache-2.0 and GPLv2 (v2.37.2, 2026-11-04); Gotify server is MIT (v3.1.1); Uptime Kuma is MIT (2.5.9); Prometheus Alertmanager is Apache-2.0 (v0.35.0, 2026-11-09)

ntfy self-hosted iOS instant delivery: with upstream-base-url set, each message triggers a poll request to an upstream APNs-connected server carrying only the message ID (X-Poll-ID) and a SHA-256 of the topic URL, with placeholder text 'New message'; the iOS app then fetches the message from the self-hosted server. Without it delivery can take hours
APNs: a notification service app extension runs only when the payload has mutable-content=1, can decrypt data sent encrypted, and has about 30 seconds to modify the payload
APNs rejects non-VoIP notification payloads larger than 4 KB (4096 bytes)
APNs token authentication needs a signing key issued from the developer's Apple account that must stay private; tokens from multiple developer accounts cannot share one connection
iOS/iPadOS 16.4 added Web Push for web apps added to the Home Screen, requested on user interaction (WebKit blog, 2023-02-16)

RFC 8030 defines Web Push with three actors: application server, a push service that delivers to user agents, and the user agent; RFC 8291 encrypts messages so the push service cannot inspect or modify them

UnifiedPush is a decentralised push system where the user picks a distributor (e.g. ntfy, NextPush, Sunup); it works on de-Googled Android and as a Linux user service (KUnifiedPush); iOS is not listed
Service Workers, Push API, Notifications, Web Authentication, WebXR Device API, Geolocation, Web Bluetooth and async Clipboard are restricted to secure contexts (HTTPS)
tailscale cert gets a Let's Encrypt certificate for a machine's MagicDNS name; machine names are published in Certificate Transparency logs, so do not enable HTTPS if names are sensitive
StartOS's CLI generates SSL certificates from a system root CA held on the server (net ssl generate-certificate)
Home Assistant Cloud remote access uses SniTun (GPL-3.0): end-to-end TLS routed by an SNI proxy over a TCP multiplexer, authenticated by a token from Nabu Casa's session master
Tauri 2.0 went stable on 2024-10-02 for macOS, Linux, Windows, iOS and Android; official plugins include biometric (Android/iOS) and barcode scanner; not all plugins work on mobile
Tauri's notification plugin documents local notifications only (no APNs/FCM remote push mention); a Tauri v3 alpha (tauri-v3.0.0-alpha.6) was released 2026-11-06
Capacitor's push-notifications plugin uses APNs on iOS (no silent push) and Firebase Cloud Messaging on Android, requiring a Firebase project's google-services.json
App Store Review Guideline 5.4: VPN apps must use NEVPNManager and may only be offered by developers enrolled as an organization; must not sell or disclose data (guidelines last updated 2026-10-16)

App Store Review Guideline 4.2.7: remote-desktop apps that mirror specific software may only connect to a user-owned PC or console on the local LAN; thin clients for cloud apps are not allowed; 4.2: apps must be more than a repackaged website

Google Play VpnService policy: VPN must be core functionality except listed categories including network tools such as remote access and parental control; a declaration form and encryption to the tunnel endpoint are required

Samba vfs_fruit provides Apple SMB client compatibility (AAPL extension); fruit:time machine = yes advertises Time Machine support and registers the share over mDNS; fruit:time machine max size caps it
Apple: Time Machine can back up to a third-party NAS over SMB; AFP is not recommended and is not supported in macOS 27 or later
W3C WebXR Device API is a Candidate Recommendation Draft dated 2026-11-09
Chrome on Android XR supports WebXR Device API, AR, Gamepads, Hit Test, Hand Input (default input), Anchors, Depth Sensing and Light Estimation; permissions persist per domain
Apple (WWDC24 session 10066): Safari on visionOS 2 supports immersive virtual-reality WebXR sessions on Vision Pro; the session does not cover immersive-ar
Samsung Galaxy XR, the first Android XR headset, launched 2025-10-21 at about US$1,799 (US and Korea first)
Omarchy (MIT) describes itself as an 'agentic Linux distribution'; its top-bar agents panel tracks Claude, Codex, Grok and other agent subscriptions and lists Hermes
Omarchy has published 72 GitHub releases since July 2025, 32 of them in the 12 months to 2026-11-10 (latest v4.5.0, 2026-11-05)
Omarchy updates via four channels (stable, RC, edge, dev); stable tracks official releases plus an Omarchy Arch mirror held one month behind upstream Arch

Omarchy shell plugins: git repos with a manifest.json (schemaVersion, id, kinds, entryPoints); the omarchy. id namespace is reserved; omarchy plugin validate runs the load-time checks; third-party plugins run as unsandboxed code with the user's rights, with only auth services kept out of reach
Bazzite (Apache-2.0) builds a rolling-yet-atomic Fedora 45 Kinoite-based image from a Containerfile and runs bootc container lint in the build

Matter onboarding QR payloads start with 'MT:' and carry version, vendor ID, product ID, commissioning flow, rendezvous methods (SoftAP, BLE, on-network, Wi-Fi PAF, NFC, Thread), a discriminator and the setup PIN
k3s supports automatically expiring agent bootstrap tokens: k3s token create --ttl (default 24h; 0 = never expires)

NATS leaf node: a server that opens an outbound connection to a remote NATS system and bridges subject interest; works with no inbound ports; the leaf joins a chosen account with a .creds file; leaves can serve further leaves (trees)
NATS gateways join independent clusters into a super-cluster with one connection per remote cluster and interest-only forwarding

Proxmox VE clusters are multi-master (any node's web UI manages all), need under 5 ms latency for corosync, need 3 nodes for reliable quorum (QDevice gives a 2-node cluster a third vote), and go read-only on quorum loss

Synology High Availability (DSM 7.4) replicates data in real time between an active and a passive server, needs two identical NAS units (mixed models only in specific cases) and a heartbeat link under 1 ms
NetBox (Apache-2.0) v4.7.5 released 2026-11-10
Lichtblick (robotics visualisation, fork of Foxglove Studio code, copyright BMW AG and Foxglove 2021-2024) is MPL-2.0, v1.30.0 (2026-10-22)
WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation dated 2024-12-12
US Revised Section 508 (E205.4, E207.2) requires WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA conformance for electronic content and software
ETSI EN 301 549 V3.2.1 is published at the ETSI deliver directory (file dated 2021-05-11); clause text not read here
Tailscale (BSD-3-Clause) latest release v1.104.6 on 2026-11-11
